units.zh: 李茂貞，深州博野人也。
units.en: Li Maozhen came from Boye in Shen Prefecture.
units.literal: Li Maozhen was a native of Boye in Shen Prefecture.

units.zh: 本姓宋，名文通，為博野軍卒，戍鳳翔。
units.en: Originally surnamed Song with the given name Wentong, he served as a soldier in the Boye Army and was posted to Fengxiang.
units.literal: His original surname was Song and his given name Wentong; he was a soldier of the Boye Army and garrisoned Fengxiang.

units.zh: 黃巢犯京師，鄭畋以博野軍擊賊，茂貞以功自隊長遷軍校。
units.en: When Huang Chao struck the capital, Zheng Tian led the Boye Army against him. Maozhen rose from squad leader to army officer for his service.
units.literal: When Huang Chao invaded the capital, Zheng Tian led the Boye Army against the rebels, and Maozhen for merit rose from squad leader to army officer.

units.zh: 光啟元年，朱玫反，僖宗出居興元。
units.en: In Guangqi 1 (885) Zhu Mei rebelled, and Emperor Xizong withdrew to Xingyuan.
units.literal: In the first year of Guangqi, Zhu Mei rebelled and Emperor Xizong went out to dwell at Xingyuan.

units.zh: 玫遣王行瑜攻大散關，茂貞與保鑾都將李鋋等敗行瑜於大唐峯。
units.en: Mei sent Wang Xingyu against Dasanguan. Maozhen and Palace Guard general Li Chan defeated him at Datang Peak.
units.literal: Mei sent Wang Xingyu to attack Dasanguan; Maozhen with Palace Guard general Li Chan and others defeated Xingyu at Datang Peak.

units.zh: 明年，玫遂敗死。
units.en: The next year Mei was defeated and killed.
units.literal: The next year Mei was defeated and died.

units.zh: 茂貞以功自扈蹕都頭拜武定軍節度使，賜以姓名。
units.en: For his service Maozhen rose from commander of the imperial escort to military commissioner of Wuding and received the surname and name by which he was known.
units.literal: Maozhen for merit rose from commander of the imperial escort to military commissioner of the Wuding Army and was granted his present surname and name.

units.zh: 扈蹕東歸，至鳳翔，鳳翔節度使李昌符與天威都頭楊守立爭道，以兵相攻，昌符不勝，走隴州。
units.en: On the eastward return to court they reached Fengxiang. Li Changfu, military commissioner of Fengxiang, and Yang Shouli, commander of Celestial Might, fought over the road. Changfu lost and fled to Longzhou.
units.literal: Escorting the emperor east on his return, they reached Fengxiang; Fengxiang military commissioner Li Changfu and Celestial Might commander Yang Shouli contended for the road and attacked each other with troops; Changfu could not prevail and fled to Long Prefecture.

units.zh: 僖宗遣茂貞擊殺昌符，以功拜鳳翔隴右節度使。
units.en: Xizong sent Maozhen to kill Changfu and, for that service, made him military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.
units.literal: Xizong sent Maozhen to strike and kill Changfu, and for merit made him military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.

units.zh: 大順元年，封隴西郡王。
units.en: In Dashun 1 (890) he was made Prince of Longxi.
units.literal: In the first year of Dashun he was enfeoffed Prince of Longxi Commandery.

units.zh: 二年，樞密使楊復恭得罪，奔於興元，興元節度使楊守亮，復恭之養子也，納之。
units.en: In the second year Yang Fugong, the Privy Council commissioner, lost the emperor’s trust and fled to Xingyuan. Yang Shouliang, military commissioner of Xingyuan and Fugong’s adopted son, took him in.
units.literal: In the second year, Privy Council Commissioner Yang Fugong fell from favor and fled to Xingyuan; the Xingyuan military commissioner Yang Shouliang, Fugong’s adopted son, received him.

units.zh: 茂貞乃上書言復恭父子罪皆當誅，因自請為山南招討使。
units.en: Maozhen memorialized that Fugong and his son deserved death, and asked to lead the campaign into the southern mountains.
units.literal: Maozhen then memorialized that father and son Fugong both deserved execution and asked to be made Southern Mountains campaign commissioner.

units.zh: 昭宗以宦者故，難之，未許。
units.en: Zhaozong, mindful of the eunuchs, hesitated and refused.
units.literal: Because of the eunuchs, Zhaozong found it difficult and did not grant it.

units.zh: 茂貞擅發兵攻破興元，復恭父子見殺。
units.en: Maozhen marched without leave, broke Xingyuan, and Fugong and his son were put to death.
units.literal: Maozhen on his own authority raised troops, stormed Xingyuan, and Fugong and his son were killed.

units.zh: 茂貞表其子繼密權知興元軍府事，昭宗乃徙茂貞山南西道節度使，以宰相徐彥若鎮鳳翔。
units.en: Maozhen asked that his son Jimi hold Xingyuan in his stead. Zhaozong moved Maozhen to Shannan West and sent Chancellor Xu Yanruo to Fengxiang.
units.literal: Maozhen memorialized that his son Jimi should temporarily oversee Xingyuan’s military administration; Zhaozong then transferred Maozhen to military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit and sent Chancellor Xu Yanruo to govern Fengxiang.

units.zh: 茂貞不奉詔，上表自論曰：「但慮軍情忽變，戎馬難羈。
units.en: Maozhen refused the order and memorialized in his own defense: “I fear only that the troops may turn restless and the cavalry slip my grip.
units.literal: Maozhen did not obey the edict and submitted a memorial arguing for himself, saying: “I only fear that army sentiment may suddenly shift and war-horses prove hard to restrain.

units.zh: 徒令甸服生靈，因茲受幣；
units.en: The heartland’s people would suffer for it—
units.literal: In vain letting the people of the royal domain suffer harm thereby;

units.zh: 未審乘輿播越，自此何之？」
units.en: and if the Son of Heaven were driven from the capital, where would he turn?”
units.literal: it is unclear where the imperial carriage in exile would go from here?”

units.zh: 昭宗以茂貞表辭不遜，不能忍，以問宰相杜讓能，讓能以謂：「茂貞地大兵強，而唐力未可以致討；
units.en: Zhaozong read insolence in the memorial and could not swallow it. He asked Chancellor Du Rangneng. Rangneng said: “Maozhen holds a wide domain and a strong army; Tang lacks the force to call him to account;
units.literal: Zhaozong, finding Maozhen’s memorial language disrespectful, could not endure it and asked Chancellor Du Rangneng; Rangneng said: “Maozhen’s territory is large and his troops strong; Tang’s strength is not yet enough to pursue punishment;

units.zh: 鳳翔又近京師，易以自危而難於後悔，佗日雖欲誅晁錯以謝諸侯，恐不能也。」
units.en: Fengxiang lies too close to Chang’an—strike at him and you court disaster you cannot undo. Another day, even if you wished to execute Chao Cuo to appease the feudal lords, you might not be able to.”
units.literal: Fengxiang is also close to the capital—easy to bring danger on oneself and hard to repent afterward; another day, even if you wished to execute Chao Cuo to appease the feudal lords, I fear you could not.”

units.zh: 昭宗怒曰：「吾不能孱孱坐受淩弱！」
units.en: Zhaozong flared: “I will not sit here and be pushed around!”
units.literal: Zhaozong angrily said: “I cannot sit weakly by and be bullied!”

units.zh: 乃責讓能治兵，而以覃王嗣周為京西招討使。
units.en: He ordered Rangneng to mobilize and made Prince of Tan Sizhou commander of the western capital campaign.
units.literal: He then rebuked Rangneng to prepare troops and made Prince of Tan Sizhou western capital campaign commissioner.

units.zh: 令下，京師市人皆知不可，相與聚承天門，遮宰相請無舉兵，爭投瓦石擊宰相，宰相下輿而走，亡其堂印，人情大恐，昭宗意益堅。
units.en: The order went out and the markets knew disaster was coming. Crowds blocked the chancellors at Chengtian Gate, begging them to halt the war, and pelted them with brick and stone until they fled on foot, leaving their seals behind. Terror swept the city, but Zhaozong only hardened his will.
units.literal: When the order went out, everyone in the capital markets knew it could not succeed; they gathered at Chengtian Gate, blocked the chancellors and begged that no troops be raised, and hurled tiles and stones at the chancellors; the chancellors left their litters and fled, losing their hall seals; popular terror was extreme, yet Zhaozong’s resolve grew firmer.

units.zh: 覃王率扈駕軍五十四都戰於盩厔，唐軍敗潰，茂貞遂犯京師，屯於三橋。
units.en: Prince of Tan Sizhou led fifty-four guard companies against Maozhen at Zhouzhi. Tang collapsed. Maozhen drove on the capital and camped at Sanqiao.
units.literal: The Prince of Tan led fifty-four companies of the imperial guard army into battle at Zhouzhi; Tang forces were routed; Maozhen then invaded the capital and encamped at Sanqiao.

units.zh: 昭宗禦安福門，殺兩樞密以謝茂貞，使罷兵。
units.en: Zhaozong appeared at the Anfu Gate, sacrificed the two Privy Council commissioners to appease Maozhen, and bade him stand down.
units.literal: Zhaozong went to the Anfu Gate, executed the two Privy Council commissioners to appease Maozhen, and ordered him to withdraw.

units.zh: 茂貞素與讓能有隙，因曰：「謀舉兵者非兩樞密，乃讓能也。」
units.en: Maozhen had long hated Rangneng. He said: “The plotters were not the Privy Council commissioners—it was Rangneng.”
units.literal: Maozhen had long borne a grudge against Rangneng and therefore said: “Those who plotted to raise troops were not the two Privy Council commissioners but Rangneng.”

units.zh: 陳兵臨臯驛，請殺讓能。
units.en: He drew up troops at Lingao Station and demanded Rangneng’s life.
units.literal: He arrayed troops at Lingao Post Station and asked that Rangneng be killed.

units.zh: 讓能曰：「臣故先言之矣，惟殺臣可以紓國難。」
units.en: Rangneng said: “I told you so from the start—kill me alone and the realm may breathe again.”
units.literal: Rangneng said: “Your servant said so from the first—only by killing your servant can the state’s peril be eased.”

units.zh: 昭宗泣下沾襟，貶讓能雷州司戶參軍，賜死，茂貞乃罷兵。
units.en: Zhaozong wept until his robe was soaked, banished Rangneng to Leizhou as registrar, and ordered him to die. Only then did Maozhen withdraw.
units.literal: Zhaozong wept until his collar was wet, demoted Rangneng to registrar of Leizhou, granted him death, and Maozhen then withdrew his troops.

units.zh: 明年，河中節度使王重盈卒，其諸子珂、珙爭立。
units.en: The next year Wang Chongying of Hezhong died, and his sons Ke and Gong fought over the circuit.
units.literal: The next year the Hezhong military commissioner Wang Chongying died; his sons Ke and Gong contended for succession.

units.zh: 晉王李克用請立珂，茂貞與韓建、王行瑜請立珙，昭宗不許。
units.en: Li Keyong of Jin backed Ke; Maozhen, Han Jian, and Wang Xingyu backed Gong. Zhaozong refused.
units.literal: Prince of Jin Li Keyong asked that Ke be installed; Maozhen with Han Jian and Wang Xingyu asked that Gong be installed; Zhaozong did not permit it.

units.zh: 茂貞等怒，率三鎮兵犯京師，謀廢昭宗，立吉王保。
units.en: Enraged, Maozhen and his allies marched from three circuits on Chang’an, plotting to depose Zhaozong and raise Prince of Ji Bao.
units.literal: Maozhen and the others were enraged, led troops from the three circuits against the capital, and plotted to depose Zhaozong and set up Prince of Ji Bao.

units.zh: 未果，而晉王亦舉兵，茂貞懼，乃殺宰相韋昭度、李磎，留其養子繼鵬以兵二千宿衛而去。
units.en: The coup failed, and Jin marched as well. Maozhen, afraid, killed Chancellors Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi, left his adopted son Jipeng with two thousand men as palace guard, and withdrew.
units.literal: They did not succeed; meanwhile the Prince of Jin also raised troops; Maozhen feared this and killed Chancellors Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi, left his adopted son Jipeng with two thousand troops as palace guard, and departed.

units.zh: 晉兵至河中，繼鵬與行瑜弟行實等爭劫昭宗出奔，京師大亂，昭宗出居於石門。
units.en: Jin reached Hezhong. Jipeng and Xingyu’s brother Xingshi fought to drag Zhaozong away. Chang’an convulsed. The emperor took refuge at Shimen.
units.literal: Jin’s army reached Hezhong; Jipeng with Xingyu’s brother Xingshi and others vied to seize Zhaozong and flee; the capital fell into great disorder; Zhaozong went out to dwell at Shimen.

units.zh: 茂貞以兵至鄠縣，斬繼鵬自贖。
units.en: Maozhen marched to E County and killed Jipeng to buy his peace.
units.literal: Maozhen with troops reached E County and beheaded Jipeng to atone.

units.zh: 晉兵已破王行瑜，還軍渭北，請擊茂貞。
units.en: Jin had crushed Wang Xingyu and, camped north of the Wei, asked leave to strike Maozhen.
units.literal: Jin’s army had already broken Wang Xingyu and, returning north of the Wei, asked to strike Maozhen.

units.zh: 昭宗以謂晉遠而茂貞近，因欲庇之以為德，而冀緩急之可恃也；
units.en: Zhaozong reckoned Jin far and Maozhen near. He meant to shelter him as a favor and keep a warlord close at hand for trouble;
units.literal: Zhaozong judged that Jin was far and Maozhen near; he therefore wished to shelter him as a kindness and hoped he might be relied on in urgency;

units.zh: 且茂貞已殺其子自贖矣，乃詔罷歸晉軍。
units.en: and Maozhen had already killed his own son in atonement. He ordered Jin to stand down.
units.literal: moreover Maozhen had already killed his son to atone; he then ordered Jin’s army to withdraw.

units.zh: 克用嘆曰：「唐不誅茂貞，憂未已也！」
units.en: Keyong sighed: “Until Tang kills Maozhen, the trouble will never end!”
units.literal: Keyong sighed and said: “If Tang does not execute Maozhen, its troubles are not ended!”

units.zh: 昭宗自石門還，益募安聖、捧宸等軍萬餘人，以諸王將之。
units.en: Zhaozong came back from Shimen and raised ten thousand more for the Ansheng and Bengchen guards, putting princes at their head.
units.literal: Zhaozong returned from Shimen and further recruited more than ten thousand men for the Ansheng and Bengchen armies, with princes as their commanders.

units.zh: 茂貞謂唐將討己，亦治兵請覲，京師大恐，居人亡入山谷。
units.en: Maozhen read the buildup as a move against him and mustered his own men to demand an audience. Chang’an panicked; people vanished into the hills.
units.literal: Maozhen thought Tang meant to attack him and also prepared troops to request an audience; the capital was greatly afraid, and residents fled into the hills and valleys.

units.zh: 茂貞遂犯京師，昭宗遣覃王拒之，覃王至三橋，軍潰，昭宗出居於華州。
units.en: Maozhen struck the capital again. Zhaozong sent Prince of Tan Sizhou to hold him at Sanqiao; the army broke. The emperor withdrew to Hua.
units.literal: Maozhen then invaded the capital; Zhaozong sent the Prince of Tan to resist him; the prince reached Sanqiao and the army collapsed; Zhaozong went out to dwell at Hua Prefecture.

units.zh: 遣宰相孫偓以兵討茂貞，韓建為茂貞請，乃已。
units.en: He sent Chancellor Sun Wo against Maozhen. Han Jian interceded, and the attack was called off.
units.literal: He sent Chancellor Sun Wo with troops to punish Maozhen; Han Jian pleaded for Maozhen, and the campaign ceased.

units.zh: 久之，加拜茂貞尚書令，封岐王。
units.en: In time Maozhen was made Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Prince of Qi.
units.literal: After a long while Maozhen was further promoted to Director of the Imperial Secretariat and enfeoffed Prince of Qi.

units.zh: 其後，昭宗為宦者所廢，既反正，宰相崔胤欲借梁兵誅諸宦者，陰與梁太祖謀之。
units.en: Later eunuchs deposed Zhaozong; after his restoration Chancellor Cui Yin sought Liang’s blades to destroy them and conspired in secret with Liang Taizu Zhu Wen.
units.literal: Later Zhaozong was deposed by eunuchs; after he was restored to the throne, Chancellor Cui Yin wished to borrow Liang troops to execute the eunuchs and secretly plotted with Liang Taizu.

units.zh: 中尉韓全誨等，亦倚茂貞之強，以為外援，茂貞遣其子繼筠以兵數千宿衛京師，宦者恃岐兵，益驕不可制。
units.en: Chief Eunuch Han Quanhui and his faction leaned on Maozhen’s power. Maozhen sent his son Jiyun with thousands of men into the capital. Backed by Qi’s army, the eunuchs grew brazen and ungovernable.
units.literal: Chief Eunuch Han Quanhui and the others also relied on Maozhen’s strength as outside support; Maozhen sent his son Jiyun with several thousand troops to guard the capital; the eunuchs, trusting in Qi troops, grew ever more arrogant and uncontrollable.

units.zh: 天復元年，胤召梁太祖以西，梁軍至同州，全誨等懼，與繼筠劫昭宗幸鳳翔。
units.en: In Tianfu 1 (901) Yin called Zhu Wen west. Liang reached Tongzhou. Quanhui and his party, terrified, joined Jiyun and dragged Zhaozong to Fengxiang.
units.literal: In the first year of Tianfu, Yin summoned Liang Taizu west; Liang troops reached Tong Prefecture; Quanhui and the others were afraid and, with Jiyun, seized Zhaozong and bore him to Fengxiang.

units.zh: 梁軍圍之逾年，茂貞每戰輒敗，閉壁不敢出。
units.en: Liang besieged Fengxiang for more than a year. Maozhen fought and lost again and again, then shut the gates and would not come out.
units.literal: Liang besieged the city for more than a year; whenever Maozhen fought he was defeated and shut the gates, not daring to come out.

units.zh: 城中薪食俱盡，自冬涉春，雨雪不止，民凍餓死者日以千數。
units.en: Wood and grain ran out. Winter dragged into spring under unending snow and rain. A thousand people a day froze or starved in the streets.
units.literal: Fuel and food in the city were exhausted; from winter into spring snow and rain did not cease; each day a thousand or more among the people died of cold and hunger.

units.zh: 米斗直錢七千，至燒人屎煮屍而食。
units.en: A dou of rice cost seven thousand cash. At last they burned nightsoil and boiled the dead for food.
units.literal: Rice reached seven thousand cash per dou; at last they burned human dung and boiled corpses to eat.

units.zh: 父自食其子，人有爭其肉者，曰：「此吾子也，汝安得而食之！」
units.en: Fathers ate their sons. Men fought over the meat, crying: “This is my child—how dare you eat him!”
units.literal: Fathers ate their own sons; some fought over the flesh, saying: “This is my son—how dare you eat him!”

units.zh: 人肉斤直錢百，狗肉斤直錢五百。
units.en: Human flesh sold for a hundred cash a pound; dog meat for five hundred.
units.literal: Human flesh was a hundred cash per jin; dog meat five hundred per jin.

units.zh: 父甘食其子，而人肉賤於狗。
units.en: Fathers ate their sons willingly, yet human flesh was cheaper than dog.
units.literal: Fathers gladly ate their sons, yet human flesh was cheaper than dog.

units.zh: 天子於宮中設小磨，遣宮人自屑豆麥以供禦，自後宮、諸王十六宅，凍餒而死者日三四。
units.en: The emperor set a hand-mill in the palace and had women grind beans and wheat for his table. In the inner quarters and the sixteen princely mansions, three or four died of cold and hunger every day.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven set up a small mill in the palace and sent palace women to grind beans and wheat themselves for the imperial table; from the rear palaces and the sixteen mansions of the princes, three or four a day died of cold and hunger.

units.zh: 城中人相與邀遮茂貞，求路以為生。
units.en: The townspeople mobbed Maozhen and begged him for a way out.
units.literal: People in the city together waylaid Maozhen and begged a way to live.

units.zh: 茂貞窮急，謀以天子與梁以為解。
units.en: Cornered, Maozhen plotted to hand the emperor to Liang to break the siege.
units.literal: Maozhen in extremity plotted to hand the Son of Heaven to Liang as the price of relief.

units.zh: 昭宗謂茂貞曰：「朕與六宮皆一日食粥，一日食不托，安能不與梁和乎？」
units.en: Zhaozong told Maozhen: “The court and I eat gruel one day and flatbread the next—how can we refuse peace with Liang?”
units.literal: Zhaozong said to Maozhen: “The six palaces and I eat porridge one day and untuo the next—how can we not make peace with Liang?”

units.zh: 三年正月，茂貞與梁約和，斬韓全誨等二十餘人，傳首梁軍，梁圍解。
units.en: In the first month of Tianfu 3 Maozhen sued for peace with Liang, beheaded Han Quanhui and twenty-odd others, and sent their heads to the besiegers. The encirclement broke.
units.literal: In the first month of the third year Maozhen made peace with Liang, beheaded Han Quanhui and more than twenty others, and sent their heads to Liang’s army; the siege was lifted.

units.zh: 天子雖得出，然梁遂劫東遷而唐亡，茂貞非惟亡唐，亦自困矣。
units.en: The emperor walked free, but Liang seized him and dragged the court east—and Tang was finished. Maozhen had ruined Tang and ruined himself.
units.literal: Though the Son of Heaven could come out, Liang then seized him and moved east—and Tang perished; Maozhen had not only destroyed Tang but trapped himself as well.

units.zh: 及梁太祖即位，諸侯之強者皆相次稱帝，獨茂貞不能，但稱岐王，開府置官屬，以妻為皇后，鳴梢羽扇視朝，出入擬天子而已。
units.en: When Zhu Wen became emperor, the great warlords one by one took imperial titles. Maozhen alone could not. He called himself Prince of Qi, opened a court, named ministers, crowned his wife, kept court with watch-drums and feather fans, and aped the Son of Heaven in little else.
units.literal: When Liang Taizu took the throne, the strongest feudal lords each in turn declared themselves emperors; only Maozhen could not; he merely styled himself Prince of Qi, opened a government and appointed officials, made his wife empress, beat the watch and used feather fans at court, and in going out and coming in imitated the Son of Heaven—that was all.

units.zh: 茂貞居岐，以寬仁愛物，民頗安之，嘗以地狹賦薄，下令搉油，因禁城門無內松薪，以其可為炬也，有優者誚之曰：「臣請並禁月明。」
units.en: Maozhen ruled Qi with a light hand and the people were fairly content. Once, taxes being thin on a narrow domain, he monopolized oil and barred pine kindling at the gates—it could be torched. A player jested: “Might I suggest we ban the moon as well?”
units.literal: Maozhen dwelt in Qi, was lenient and loved the people, and the folk were rather at peace; once, because the land was narrow and taxes thin, he ordered a monopoly on oil and forbade bringing pine fuel through the gates, since it could be made into torches; a performer mocked him, saying: “Your servant begs that moonlight be forbidden as well.”

units.zh: 茂貞笑而不怒。
units.en: Maozhen laughed and let it pass.
units.literal: Maozhen laughed and was not angry.

units.zh: 初，茂貞破楊守亮取興元，而邠、寧、鄜坊皆附之，有地二十州，其被梁圍也，興元入於蜀；
units.en: When Maozhen had crushed Yang Shouliang and taken Xingyuan, Bin, Ning, and Yan-Yan all came in—twenty prefectures in all. Under Liang’s siege Xingyuan went to Shu;
units.literal: Earlier, when Maozhen broke Yang Shouliang and took Xingyuan, Bin, Ning, and Yan-Yan circuits all submitted to him and he held twenty prefectures; when he was besieged by Liang, Xingyuan fell to Shu;

units.zh: 開平已後，邠、寧、鄜、坊入於梁，秦、鳳、階、成又入於蜀；
units.en: after Kaiping, Bin, Ning, Yan, and Yan fell to Liang; Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng to Shu again;
units.literal: after Kaiping, Bin, Ning, Yan, and Yan fell to Liang; Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng again fell to Shu;

units.zh: 當梁末年，所有七州而已。
units.en: by Liang’s end he held seven prefectures only.
units.literal: by Liang’s last years he held only seven prefectures.

units.zh: 二十州者：岐、隴、涇、原、渭、武、秦、成、階、鳳、邠、寧、慶、衍、鄜、坊、丹、延、梁、洋也。
units.en: The twenty prefectures were Qi, Long, Jing, Yuan, Wei, Wu, Qin, Cheng, Jie, Feng, Bin, Ning, Qing, Yan, Fu, Fang, Dan, Yan, Liang, and Yang.
units.literal: The twenty prefectures were Qi, Long, Jing, Yuan, Wei, Wu, Qin, Cheng, Jie, Feng, Bin, Ning, Qing, Yan, Fu, Fang, Dan, Yan, Liang, and Yang.

units.zh: 莊宗已破梁，茂貞稱岐王，上箋以季父行自處。
units.en: Once Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Maozhen still called himself Prince of Qi and addressed Tang as a junior kinsman to an elder uncle.
units.literal: After Zhuangzong had broken Liang, Maozhen styled himself Prince of Qi and in memorials treated himself as the emperor’s junior uncle by age.

units.zh: 及聞入洛，乃上表稱臣，遣其子從嚴來朝。
units.en: Hearing that Zhuangzong had entered Luoyang, he submitted as a subject and sent his son Congyan to court.
units.literal: When he heard of the entry into Luoyang he then submitted a memorial declaring himself a subject and sent his son Congyan to court.

units.zh: 莊宗以其耆老，甚尊禮之，改封秦王，詔書不名。
units.en: Zhuangzong, honoring his age, changed his title to Prince of Qin and wrote edicts without naming him.
units.literal: Zhuangzong, because he was old, honored him greatly, changed his enfeoffment to Prince of Qin, and in edicts did not write his personal name.

units.zh: 同光二年，以疾卒，年六十九，謚曰忠敬。
units.en: In Tongguang 2 (924) he died at sixty-nine, posthumously Loyal and Respectful.
units.literal: In the second year of Tongguang he died of illness at sixty-nine; posthumous title Loyal and Respectful.

units.zh: 從嚴為人柔而善書畫，茂貞承制拜從嚴彰義軍節度使。
units.en: Congyan was mild and skilled in calligraphy and painting. Maozhen had him appointed military commissioner of Zhangyi by imperial order.
units.literal: Congyan was gentle by nature and skilled at calligraphy and painting; Maozhen by imperial order made Congyan military commissioner of Zhangyi.

units.zh: 茂貞卒，拜鳳翔節度使。
units.en: At Maozhen’s death Congyan succeeded him at Fengxiang.
units.literal: When Maozhen died, Congyan was made military commissioner of Fengxiang.

units.zh: 魏王繼岌征蜀，為供軍轉運應接使。
units.en: When Prince of Wei Jiye marched on Shu, Congyan served as supply and transport liaison commissioner.
units.literal: When Prince of Wei Jiye campaigned against Shu, Congyan served as supply and transport liaison commissioner.

units.zh: 蜀平，繼岌遣從嚴部送王衍，行至鳳翔，監軍使柴重厚拒而不納，從嚴遂東至華州，聞莊宗之難乃西歸。
units.en: When Shu fell, Jiye put Congyan in charge of escorting Wang Yan. At Fengxiang, Military Supervisor Chai Zhonghou shut the gates on him. Congyan went east to Hua, then turned west on news of Zhuangzong’s peril.
units.literal: When Shu fell, Jiye sent Congyan to escort Wang Yan; reaching Fengxiang, Military Supervisor Chai Zhonghou refused him entry; Congyan therefore went east to Hua Prefecture, and hearing of Zhuangzong’s crisis turned back west.

units.zh: 明宗入立，聞重厚嘗拒從嚴，遣人誅之。
units.en: When Mingzong took the throne he learned Zhonghou had barred Congyan and sent men to kill him.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he heard that Zhonghou had once refused Congyan and sent men to execute him.

units.zh: 從嚴上書，言重厚守鳳翔，軍民無所擾，願貸其過。
units.en: Congyan wrote that Zhonghou had held Fengxiang without troubling troops or people and asked mercy for him.
units.literal: Congyan memorialized that Zhonghou had held Fengxiang without disturbing soldiers or people and begged that his offense be pardoned.

units.zh: 雖不許，士人以此多之。
units.en: The pardon was denied, but men of letters praised Congyan for it.
units.literal: Though the request was not granted, scholars for this held Congyan in high regard.

units.zh: 歷鎮宣武、天平。
units.en: He later held Xuanyi and Tianping.
units.literal: He successively governed Xuanyi and Tianping.

units.zh: 從嚴有田千頃、竹千畝在鳳翔，懼侵民利，未嘗省理，鳳翔人愛之。
units.en: Congyan owned a thousand qing of land and a thousand mu of bamboo at Fengxiang. Fearing he would burden the people, he never went to collect from them, and Fengxiang loved him for it.
units.literal: Congyan had a thousand qing of fields and a thousand mu of bamboo at Fengxiang; fearing harm to the people’s interest, he never went to oversee them, and the people of Fengxiang loved him.

units.zh: 廢帝起鳳翔，將行，鳳翔人叩馬乞從嚴。
units.en: When Feidi raised his banner in Fengxiang and prepared to leave, the townspeople caught his horse and begged for Congyan.
units.literal: When Feidi rose in Fengxiang and was about to depart, the people of Fengxiang seized his horse and begged for Congyan.

units.zh: 廢帝入立，復以從嚴為鳳翔節度使，卒年四十九。
units.en: When Feidi became emperor he restored Congyan to Fengxiang. Congyan died at forty-nine.
units.literal: When Feidi took the throne he again made Congyan military commissioner of Fengxiang; Congyan died at forty-nine.

units.zh: 韓建，字佐時，許州長社人也。
units.en: Han Jian, styled Zuoshi, came from Changshe in Xu Prefecture.
units.literal: Han Jian, styled Zuoshi, was a native of Changshe in Xu Prefecture.

units.zh: 少為蔡州軍校，隸忠武軍將鹿晏弘。
units.en: As a youth he was an officer in Cai’s army under Lu Yanhong of Zhongwu.
units.literal: In youth he was an officer in Cai Prefecture’s army and served under Zhongwu general Lu Yanhong.

units.zh: 從楊復光攻黃巢於長安，巢已破，復光亦死，晏弘與建等無所屬，乃以麾下兵西迎僖宗於蜀，所過攻劫。
units.en: He followed Yang Fuguang against Huang Chao at Chang’an. When Chao fell and Fuguang died, Yanhong and Jian were left masterless. They marched west to fetch Emperor Xizong from Shu, looting every mile.
units.literal: Following Yang Fuguang he attacked Huang Chao at Chang’an; when Chao was broken Fuguang also died; Yanhong and Jian and the rest had nowhere to belong; they therefore led their troops west to welcome Emperor Xizong in Shu, plundering wherever they passed.

units.zh: 行至興元，逐牛叢，據山南。
units.en: At Xingyuan they drove out Niu Cong and seized the southern mountains.
units.literal: Reaching Xingyuan they drove out Niu Cong and seized the southern mountains.

units.zh: 已而不能守，晏弘東走許州，建乃奔於蜀，拜金吾衛將軍。
units.en: They could not hold the ground. Yanhong fled east to Xu; Jian went to Shu and was made a Gold Crow Guard general.
units.literal: Before long they could not hold it; Yanhong went east to Xu Prefecture; Jian then fled to Shu and was made a Gold Crow Guard general.

units.zh: 僖宗還長安，建為潼關防禦使、華州刺史。
units.en: When Xizong returned to Chang’an, Jian became Tong Pass defense commissioner and governor of Hua.
units.literal: When Xizong returned to Chang’an, Jian became Tong Pass defense commissioner and Hua Prefecture governor.

units.zh: 華州數經大兵，戶口流散，建少賤，習農事，乃披荊棘，督民耕植，出入閭里，問其疾苦。
units.en: Hua had been ravaged again and again; the people had fled. Jian, raised poor and knowing the soil, cleared the scrub, drove the farmers back to the plow, and walked the lanes asking after their wants.
units.literal: Hua had repeatedly suffered great armies; households scattered; Jian in youth had been lowly and knew farming; he therefore cleared brambles, urged the people to plow and plant, and went in and out of lanes asking after their hardships.

units.zh: 建初不知書，乃使人題其所服器皿床榻，為其名目以視之，久乃漸通文字。
units.en: Jian could not read at first. He had his bowls, beds, and tables marked with their names until, slowly, he learned the script.
units.literal: At first Jian did not know writing; he had people label the vessels, bedframes, and tables he used with their names so he could recognize them; after a long while he gradually came to know characters.

units.zh: 見《玉篇》，喜曰：「吾以類求之，何所不得也。」
units.en: He opened the Yupian and exclaimed: “Seek by category—what can I not find?”
units.literal: Seeing the Yupian he rejoiced and said: “If I seek by category, what can I not find?”

units.zh: 因以通音韻聲偶，暇則課學書史。
units.en: He taught himself rhyme and tone, and in his spare hours studied history.
units.literal: He thereby mastered rhyme and tonal patterns, and in spare time studied histories.

units.zh: 是時，天下已亂，諸鎮皆武夫，獨建撫緝兵民，又好學。
units.en: The realm was already broken; every circuit had a warlord—only Jian soothed his soldiers and people and loved books besides.
units.literal: At that time the realm was already in disorder; every circuit had a warrior chief—only Jian comforted soldiers and people and also loved learning.

units.zh: 荊南成汭時冒姓郭，亦善緝荊楚。
units.en: Cheng Rui of Jingnan then falsely took the surname Guo and was likewise skilled at pacifying Jing-Chu.
units.literal: Cheng Rui of Jingnan at the time falsely bore the surname Guo and was also skilled at settling Jing-Chu.

units.zh: 當時號為「北韓南郭」。
units.en: Men called them “Han in the north, Guo in the south.”
units.literal: At the time they were called “Han in the north, Guo in the south.”

units.zh: 大順元年，以兵屬張濬伐晉，濬敗，建自含山遯歸。
units.en: In Dashun 1 (890) he lent his troops to Zhang Jun’s campaign against Jin. Jun was beaten, and Jian fled back from Hanshan.
units.literal: In the first year of Dashun he placed his troops under Zhang Jun to campaign against Jin; Jun was defeated, and Jian fled back from Hanshan.

units.zh: 河中王重盈死，諸子珂、珙爭立，晉人助珂，建與王行瑜、李茂貞助珙。
units.en: When Wang Chongying of Hezhong died, his sons Ke and Gong fought over the circuit. Jin backed Ke; Jian, Wang Xingyu, and Li Maozhen backed Gong.
units.literal: Wang Chongying of Hezhong died; his sons Ke and Gong contended for succession; Jin supported Ke, and Jian with Wang Xingyu and Li Maozhen supported Gong.

units.zh: 昭宗不許，建等大怒，以三鎮兵犯京師。
units.en: Zhaozong refused. Jian and his allies, furious, marched on the capital from three circuits.
units.literal: Zhaozong did not permit it; Jian and the others were greatly enraged and led troops from the three circuits against the capital.

units.zh: 昭宗見建等責之，行瑜、茂貞惶恐戰汗不能語，獨建前自陳述。
units.en: Zhaozong confronted Jian and his allies and rebuked them. Xingyu and Maozhen shook with fear and could not speak. Only Jian stepped forward to plead his case.
units.literal: Zhaozong received Jian and the others and reproached them; Xingyu and Maozhen were afraid, trembling and sweating, and could not speak; only Jian stepped forward and spoke for himself.

units.zh: 乃殺宰相韋昭度、李磎等，謀廢昭宗。
units.en: They killed Chancellors Wei Zhaodu and Li Xi and plotted to depose Zhaozong.
units.literal: They then killed Chancellors Wei Zhaodu, Li Xi, and others and plotted to depose Zhaozong.

units.zh: 會晉舉兵且至，建等懼，乃還。
units.en: Jin was marching too, and Jian and his allies, afraid, pulled back.
units.literal: Just then Jin also raised troops and was about to arrive; Jian and the others were afraid and withdrew.

units.zh: 晉兵問罪三鎮，兵傅華州，建登城呼曰：「弊邑未常失禮於大國，何為見攻？」
units.en: Jin pressed the three circuits and besieged Hua. Jian mounted the wall and shouted: “My city has never slighted your great state—why attack us?”
units.literal: Jin’s army demanded satisfaction from the three circuits; troops pressed Hua Prefecture; Jian mounted the wall and called out: “My little city has never been disrespectful to your great state—why are we attacked?”

units.zh: 晉人曰：「君以兵犯天子，殺大臣，是以討也。」
units.en: Jin answered: “You marched on the emperor and killed his ministers. That is why we fight you.”
units.literal: The men of Jin said: “You led troops against the Son of Heaven and killed great ministers—that is why you are punished.”

units.zh: 已而與晉和。
units.en: Soon afterward they made peace with Jin.
units.literal: Before long they made peace with Jin.

units.zh: 乾寧三年，李茂貞復犯京師，昭宗將奔太原，次渭北，建遣子允請幸華州。
units.en: In Qianning 3 (896) Maozhen struck Chang’an again. Zhaozong meant to flee to Taiyuan and halted north of the Wei. Jian sent his son Yun to beg him to come to Hua.
units.literal: In the third year of Qianning, Li Maozhen again invaded the capital; Zhaozong was about to flee to Taiyuan and, halting north of the Wei, Jian sent his son Yun to ask that the emperor visit Hua Prefecture.

units.zh: 昭宗又欲如鄜州，建追及昭宗於富平，泣曰：「藩臣倔強，非止茂貞，若舍近畿而巡極塞，乘輿渡河，不可復矣！」
units.en: Zhaozong thought to go on to Yan. Jian overtook him at Fuping and wept: “The warlords are proud—Maozhen is not the only one. Leave the heartland for the far border, cross the river, and you will never come back!”
units.literal: Zhaozong also wished to go to Yan Prefecture; Jian caught up with Zhaozong at Fuping and wept, saying: “Feudal lords are stubborn—not Maozhen alone; if you leave the near capital to tour the far frontier, once the imperial carriage crosses the river it cannot return!”

units.zh: 昭宗亦泣，遂幸華州。
units.en: Zhaozong wept too, and turned aside to Hua.
units.literal: Zhaozong wept as well and therefore visited Hua Prefecture.

units.zh: 是時，天子孤弱，獨有殿後軍及定州三都將李筠等兵千餘人為衛，以諸王將之。
units.en: The emperor stood alone and weak. Only the Rear Guard and Li Yun’s three Dingzhou companies—a thousand men or so—shielded him, led by princes.
units.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was isolated and weak; only the Rear Guard army and the three Dingzhou companies under Li Yun and others—little more than a thousand troops—served as escort, with princes as commanders.

units.zh: 建已得昭宗幸其鎮，遂欲制之，因請罷諸王將兵，散去殿後諸軍，累表不報。
units.en: Once Zhaozong was on his ground, Jian meant to cage him. He asked that princes be stripped of command and the Rear Guard dissolved. Memorial after memorial went unanswered.
units.literal: Jian, having gained Zhaozong’s visit to his circuit, then wished to control him; he therefore asked that the princes be removed from command and the Rear Guard and other armies be disbanded; memorial after memorial went unanswered.

units.zh: 昭宗登齊雲樓，西北顧望京師，作《菩薩蠻辭》三章以思歸，其卒章曰：「野煙生碧樹，陌上行人去。
units.en: Zhaozong climbed Qiyun Tower, gazed northwest toward Chang’an, and wrote three stanzas of “Bodhisattva Barbarian” yearning for home. The last runs: “Wild smoke climbs from green trees; strangers on the road pass by.
units.literal: Zhaozong ascended Qiyun Tower, looked northwest toward the capital, and composed three stanzas of “Bodhisattva Barbarian” lyrics longing to return; the closing stanza says: “Wild smoke rises from green trees; travelers on the road depart.

units.zh: 安得有英雄，迎歸大內中？」
units.en: Where is the hero who will bring me home to the Inner Court?”
units.literal: Where is there a hero to welcome me back within the Great Within?”

units.zh: 酒酣，與從臣悲歌泣下，建與諸王皆屬和之。
units.en: Deep in wine he and his court sang until they wept. Jian and the princes took up the refrain.
units.literal: When wine was deep he and his followers sang in grief until they wept; Jian and the princes all joined in the harmony.

units.zh: 建心尤不悅，因遣人告諸王謀殺建、劫天子幸佗鎮。
units.en: Jian’s mood turned darker still. He sent word that the princes plotted to murder him and drag the emperor to another warlord.
units.literal: Jian’s heart was especially displeased; he therefore sent men to report that the princes plotted to kill Jian and seize the Son of Heaven to flee to another circuit.

units.zh: 昭宗召建，將辨之，建稱疾不出，乃遣諸王自詣，建不見。
units.en: Zhaozong summoned Jian to answer the charge. Jian pleaded illness and stayed away. He made the princes come to his door. Jian refused them.
units.literal: Zhaozong summoned Jian to argue the matter; Jian claimed illness and would not come out; he then sent the princes themselves to call on him; Jian would not see them.

units.zh: 請送諸王十六宅，昭宗難之。
units.en: He demanded the princes be confined in the Sixteen Mansions. Zhaozong balked.
units.literal: He asked that the princes be sent to the Sixteen Mansions; Zhaozong found it hard to agree.

units.zh: 建乃率精兵數千圍行宮，請誅李筠。
units.en: Jian surrounded the traveling palace with picked troops and demanded Li Yun’s head.
units.literal: Jian then led several thousand picked troops to surround the traveling palace and asked that Li Yun be executed.

units.zh: 昭宗大懼，遽詔斬筠，悉散殿後及三都衛兵，幽諸王於十六宅。
units.en: Terrified, Zhaozong ordered Yun killed at once, broke up the Rear Guard and the three capital companies, and walled the princes in the Sixteen Mansions.
units.literal: Zhaozong was greatly afraid and at once ordered Yun beheaded, fully disbanded the Rear Guard and the three capital guard companies, and imprisoned the princes in the Sixteen Mansions.

units.zh: 昭宗益悔幸華，遣延王戒丕使於晉，以謀興復。
units.en: Zhaozong bitterly regretted Hua and sent Prince of Yan Jiepi to Jin to plot his restoration.
units.literal: Zhaozong regretted ever more having visited Hua and sent Prince of Yan Jiepi as envoy to Jin to plot restoration.

units.zh: 戒丕還，建與中尉劉季述誣諸王謀反，以兵圍十六宅，諸王皆登屋叫呼，遂見殺。
units.en: When Jiepi returned, Jian and Chief Eunuch Liu Jishu accused the princes of treason, ringed the Sixteen Mansions with troops, and cut them down as they screamed from the rooftops.
units.literal: When Jiepi returned, Jian with Chief Eunuch Liu Jishu falsely charged the princes with plotting rebellion, surrounded the Sixteen Mansions with troops; the princes all climbed to the roofs and cried out—and were then killed.

units.zh: 昭宗無如之何，為建立德政碑以慰安之。
units.en: Zhaozong was powerless to stop it and raised a monument to Han Jian’s “virtuous rule” to soothe him.
units.literal: Zhaozong could do nothing about it and had a monument to Jian’s virtuous government erected to comfort him.

units.zh: 建已殺諸王，乃營南莊，起樓閣，欲邀昭宗遊幸，因以廢之而立德王裕。
units.en: After killing the princes, Jian built the Southern Villa with towers and pavilions, hoping to lure Zhaozong on a visit, depose him, and raise Prince of De Yu.
units.literal: Jian had already killed the princes; he then built the Southern Villa and raised towers and pavilions, wishing to invite Zhaozong on an excursion so as to depose him and set up Prince of De Yu.

units.zh: 其父叔豐謂建曰：「汝陳、許間一田夫爾，遭時之亂，蒙天子厚恩至此，欲以兩州百里之地行大事，覆族之禍，吾不忍見，不如先死！」
units.en: His father Shufeng told him: “You were a farmer between Chen and Xu. In these troubled times the emperor raised you this high. To attempt a coup with two prefectures and a hundred li is to invite the ruin of our whole clan. I cannot watch it—let me die first!”
units.literal: His father Shufeng said to Jian: “You were only a farmer between Chen and Xu; in the disorder of the times you received the Son of Heaven’s great favor to reach this point; yet you wish to attempt a great affair with a domain of two prefectures and a hundred li—the calamity of exterminating the clan—I cannot bear to see it; better to die first!”

units.zh: 因泣下歔欷。
units.en: He wept aloud.
units.literal: He then wept and sobbed.

units.zh: 李茂貞、梁太祖皆欲發兵迎天子，建稍恐懼，乃止。
units.en: Li Maozhen and Liang Taizu both prepared to march and rescue the emperor. Jian grew afraid and dropped the plan.
units.literal: Li Maozhen and Liang Taizu both wished to raise troops to welcome the Son of Heaven back; Jian grew somewhat afraid and stopped.

units.zh: 光化元年，昭宗還長安，自為建畫像，封建潁川郡王，賜以鐵券。
units.en: In Guanghua 1 (898) Zhaozong returned to Chang’an, painted Jian’s portrait himself, made him Prince of Yingchuan, and granted him an iron certificate of mercy.
units.literal: In the first year of Guanghua, Zhaozong returned to Chang’an, personally painted Jian’s portrait, enfeoffed him Prince of Yingchuan Commandery, and granted him an iron certificate.

units.zh: 建辭王爵，乃封建許國公。
units.en: Jian refused the princely title and was made Duke of Xu instead.
units.literal: Jian declined the princely rank and was therefore enfeoffed Duke of Xu.

units.zh: 梁太祖以兵向長安，遣張存敬攻同州，建判官司馬鄴以城降，太祖使鄴召建，建乃出降。
units.en: Liang Taizu marched on Chang’an and sent Zhang Cunjing against Tong. Jian’s judge Sima Ye opened the gates. Taizu sent Ye to call Jian out, and Jian surrendered.
units.literal: Liang Taizu marched on Chang’an, sent Zhang Cunjing to attack Tong Prefecture; Jian’s judge Sima Ye surrendered the city; Taizu had Ye summon Jian, and Jian then came out and submitted.

units.zh: 太祖責建背己，建曰：「判官李巨川之謀也。」
units.en: Taizu accused Jian of betrayal. Jian said, “Judge Li Juchuan talked me into it.”
units.literal: Taizu reproached Jian for turning against him; Jian said: “It was Judge Li Juchuan’s plan.”

units.zh: 太祖怒，即殺巨川，以建從行。
units.en: Taizu flew into a rage, killed Juchuan on the spot, and kept Jian with the army.
units.literal: Taizu was enraged and at once killed Juchuan, and had Jian accompany the march.

units.zh: 昭宗東遷，建從至洛，昭宗舉酒屬太祖與建曰：「遷都之後，國步小康，社稷安危，系卿兩人。」
units.en: When Zhaozong moved east, Jian went with him to Luoyang. The emperor raised his cup to Taizu and Jian: “Since we left Chang’an the realm has steadied a little. The throne rests on you two.”
units.literal: When Zhaozong moved east, Jian followed to Luoyang; Zhaozong raised a cup and charged Taizu and Jian: “After the move of the capital, the realm has known a little peace; the safety of the altars rests on you two.”

units.zh: 次何皇后舉觴，建躡太祖足，太祖乃陽醉去。
units.en: Then Empress He offered wine. Jian stepped on Taizu’s foot; Taizu pretended to be drunk and walked out.
units.literal: Next Empress He raised her goblet; Jian trod on Taizu’s foot, and Taizu then feigned drunkenness and left.

units.zh: 建出，謂太祖曰：「天子與宮人眼語，幕下有兵仗聲，恐公不免也。」
units.en: Outside, Jian told Taizu: “The emperor was signaling the women with his eyes. I heard weapons under the curtain. They mean to kill you.”
units.literal: Jian went out and said to Taizu: “The Son of Heaven was speaking with the palace women by eye; under the curtain there was the sound of arms—your life may not be spared.”

units.zh: 太祖以故尤德之，表建平盧軍節度使。
units.en: Taizu owed him his life and made him military commissioner of Pinglu.
units.literal: For this Taizu was all the more grateful and memorialized Jian as military commissioner of Pinglu.

units.zh: 太祖即位，拜司徒同中書門下平章事。
units.en: When Taizu became emperor, Jian was made Minister of Works and open-folder chancellor.
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Jian was appointed Minister of Works and co-equal with the Secretariat-Chancellery.

units.zh: 太祖性剛暴，臣下莫敢諫諍，惟建時有言，太祖亦優容之。
units.en: Taizu was brutal; no one else dared speak plainly. Only Jian would venture a word, and Taizu usually let it pass.
units.literal: Taizu’s nature was harsh and violent; subordinates dared not remonstrate—only Jian sometimes spoke, and Taizu also treated him with forbearance.

units.zh: 太祖郊於洛，建為大禮使。
units.en: When Taizu sacrificed at the suburbs of Luoyang, Jian directed the rites.
units.literal: When Taizu performed suburban rites at Luoyang, Jian was grand ritual commissioner.

units.zh: 罷相，出鎮許州，太祖崩，許州軍亂，見殺，年五十八。
units.en: Stripped of the seal, he took Xu Prefecture. When Taizu died the Xu garrison rose and killed him. He was fifty-eight.
units.literal: Removed from the chancellery, he went out to govern Xu Prefecture; when Taizu died, Xu’s army mutinied and he was killed, aged fifty-eight.

units.zh: 李仁福
units.en: Li Renfu
units.literal: Li Renfu

units.zh: 李仁福，不知其世家。
units.en: Of Li Renfu’s family nothing is recorded.
units.literal: Li Renfu—his lineage is unknown.

units.zh: 當唐僖宗時，有拓拔思敬者，為夏州偏將，後以與破黃巢功，賜姓李氏，拜夏州節度使。
units.en: Under Xizong a man named Tuoba Sijing was a deputy in Xia. For helping crush Huang Chao he took the imperial surname Li and became commissioner of Xia.
units.literal: In the time of Emperor Xizong of Tang there was one Tuoba Sijing, a deputy general of Xia Prefecture; later for merit in breaking Huang Chao he was granted the surname Li and appointed military commissioner of Xia.

units.zh: 思敬卒，乾寧二年，以其弟思諫為節度使。
units.en: Sijing died. In Qianning 2 his brother Sijian succeeded him at Xia.
units.literal: Sijing died; in the second year of Qianning his younger brother Sijian was made military commissioner.

units.zh: 自唐末天下大亂，史官實錄多闕，諸鎮因時倔起，自非有大善惡暴著於世者，不能紀其始終。
units.en: Late Tang chaos left the historians’ records in tatters. Petty warlords sprang up everywhere; unless a man’s deeds were glaring, no one could trace his rise and fall.
units.literal: From the late Tang the realm fell into great disorder; veritable records of the historians were often missing; circuits rose in their season, and unless great good or evil stood plain before the world, beginning and end could not be chronicled.

units.zh: 是時，興元、鳳翔、邠寧、鄜坊、河中、同華諸鎮之兵，四面並起而交爭，獨靈夏未嘗為唐患，而亦無大功。
units.en: Armies from Xingyuan, Fengxiang, Binning, Bianfang, Hezhong, and Tonghua clashed on every side. Only Ling and Xia stayed out of Tang’s wars—and out of its glory.
units.literal: At that time the armies of Xingyuan, Fengxiang, Binning, Bianfang, Hezhong, and Tonghua rose on four sides and fought one another; only Ling and Xia never troubled Tang, yet won no great merit either.

units.zh: 朱玫之亂，思敬與鄜州李思孝皆以兵屯渭橋。
units.en: During Zhu Mei’s revolt, Sijing and Li Sixiao of Fu Prefecture encamped at Wei Bridge.
units.literal: In Zhu Mei’s rebellion, Sijing and Li Sixiao of Fu Prefecture both camped their troops at Wei Bridge.

units.zh: 其後，黃巢陷京師，王重榮、李克用等會諸鎮兵討賊，思敬與破巢復京師，然皆未嘗有所可稱，故思敬之世次、功過不顯而無傳。
units.en: When Chao seized Chang’an, Wang Chongrong and Li Keyong mustered the circuits against him. Sijing helped retake the city, but won no fame for it. His deeds and his line fade into silence.
units.literal: Afterward, when Huang Chao took the capital, Wang Chongrong, Li Keyong, and others joined circuit armies to punish the bandits; Sijing helped break Chao and recover the capital—yet none ever won particular praise, so Sijing’s generation, merit, and fault do not stand out and have no separate account.

units.zh: 梁開平二年，思諫卒，軍中立其子彜昌為留後，梁即拜彜昌節度使。
units.en: In Liang Kaiping 2 Sijian died. The troops made his son Yizichang acting commissioner, and Liang confirmed him.
units.literal: In the second year of Kaiping of Liang, Sijian died; the army set up his son Yizichang as acting commissioner, and Liang at once appointed Yizichang military commissioner.

units.zh: 明年，其將高宗益作亂，殺彜昌。
units.en: The next year his general Gao Zongyi mutinied and killed Yizichang.
units.literal: The next year his general Gao Zongyi rebelled and killed Yizichang.

units.zh: 是時，仁福為蕃部指揮使，戍兵於外，軍中乃迎仁福立之，不知其於思諫為親疏也。
units.en: Renfu was then a tribal commandant on frontier duty. The garrison brought him in and made him ruler; no one knew how he stood to Sijian.
units.literal: At that time Renfu was a tribal commandant; he was garrisoned outside, and the army then welcomed Renfu and set him up—whether he was near or distant kin to Sijian was not known.

units.zh: 是歲四月，拜仁福檢校司空、定難軍節度使。
units.en: That fourth month Renfu was made Acting Minister of Works and commissioner of the Dingnan army.
units.literal: In the fourth month of that year Renfu was appointed Acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of the Dingnan army.

units.zh: 終梁之世，奉正朔而已。
units.en: For all of Liang’s reign he did no more than keep the calendar.
units.literal: Through Liang’s age he merely observed the court calendar.

units.zh: 是時，岐王李茂貞，晉王李克用，數會兵攻仁福，梁輒出兵救之。
units.en: Li Maozhen of Qi and Li Keyong of Jin attacked him again and again; Liang marched to his aid each time.
units.literal: At that time the Qi Prince Li Maozhen and the Jin Prince Li Keyong several times joined forces to attack Renfu, and Liang each time sent troops to rescue him.

units.zh: 仁福累官至檢校太師兼中書令，封朔方王。
units.en: Renfu rose to Acting Grand Preceptor, open-folder chancellor, and Prince of Shuofang.
units.literal: Renfu rose in office to Acting Grand Preceptor and co-equal with the Secretariat-Chancellery, and was enfeoffed Prince of Shuofang.

units.zh: 長興四年三月卒，其子彜超自立為留後。
units.en: In Changxing 4, third month, he died. His son Yichao made himself acting commissioner.
units.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Changxing he died; his son Yichao set himself up as acting commissioner.

units.zh: 自仁福時，邊將多言仁福通於契丹，恐為邊患。
units.en: From Renfu’s day border commanders whispered that he courted the Khitan and would one day bite the realm.
units.literal: From Renfu’s time, frontier generals often said Renfu was in league with the Khitan and might become a border scourge.

units.zh: 明宗因其卒，乃以彜超為延州刺史、彰武軍節度使，而徙彰武安從進代之。
units.en: On Renfu’s death Mingzong named Yichao commissioner of Yan and the Zhangwu army, and sent An Congjin of Zhangwu to take Xia.
units.literal: Because he had died, Mingzong made Yichao military commissioner of Yanzhou and the Zhangwu army, and moved Zhangwu’s An Congjin to replace him.

units.zh: 恐彜超不受代，遣邠州藥彥稠以兵五萬送從進之鎮。
units.en: Lest Yichao refuse the transfer, Mingzong sent Yao Yanchou of Bin with fifty thousand men to install Congjin.
units.literal: Fearing Yichao would refuse transfer, he sent Yao Yanchou of Bin with fifty thousand men to escort Congjin to his post.

units.zh: 彜超果不受代，從進與彥稠以兵圍之，百餘日不克。
units.en: Yichao would not yield. Congjin and Yanchou besieged him for a hundred days and could not break in.
units.literal: Yichao indeed would not accept replacement; Congjin and Yanchou besieged him for more than a hundred days without taking the city.

units.zh: 夏州城壁素堅，故老傳言赫連勃勃蒸土築之，從進等穴地道，至城下堅如鐵石，鑿不能入。
units.en: Xia’s walls were legendary—old men said Helian Bobo had steamed the earth to raise them. The besiegers dug a mine to the foot of the wall and struck iron-hard stone they could not cut.
units.literal: Xia’s walls had always been strong; elders said Helian Bobo had steamed earth to build them; Congjin and the rest tunneled to beneath the wall—it was hard as iron and stone, and they could not bore through.

units.zh: 彜超外招党項，抄掠從進等糧道，自陜以西，民運鬥粟束芻，其費數千，人不堪命，道路愁苦。
units.en: Yichao rallied Tangut allies to cut their supplies. West of Shaan every peck and bundle cost a fortune; the people buckled under the levy and the roads filled with lament.
units.literal: Yichao called in the Tangut from outside and raided the supply lines of Congjin and the rest; from west of Shaan the people carried a peck of grain and a bundle of fodder at costs of thousands—men could not bear the burden, and the roads groaned with misery.

units.zh: 明宗遂釋不攻，以彜超為定難軍節度使。
units.en: Mingzong lifted the siege and let Yichao keep the Dingnan commission.
units.literal: Mingzong then ceased the attack and made Yichao military commissioner of the Dingnan army.

units.zh: 清泰二年卒。
units.en: He died in Qingtai 2.
units.literal: In the second year of Qingtai he died.

units.zh: 其弟彜興，累官檢校太師兼侍中，周顯德中，封西平王，其後事具國史。
units.en: His brother Yixing became Acting Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant, was made Prince of Xiping under Zhou Xiande, and passes from this account into the official histories.
units.literal: His younger brother Yixing rose to Acting Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant; in the Xiande era of Zhou he was enfeoffed Prince of Xiping; his later career is in the dynastic histories.

units.zh: ○韓遜
units.en: ○ Han Xun
units.literal: ○ Han Xun

units.zh: 韓遜，不知其世家。
units.en: Of Han Xun’s family nothing is recorded.
units.literal: Han Xun—his lineage is unknown.

units.zh: 初為靈武軍校，當唐末之亂，據有靈鹽，唐即以為節度使，而史失不錄，不見其事。
units.en: He began as an officer at Lingwu. When Tang collapsed he seized Ling and Salt and Tang named him commissioner—but the record is lost and his story vanished.
units.literal: At first he was an officer of the Lingwu army; in the disorder at the end of Tang he seized Ling and Salt, and Tang then made him military commissioner—yet the histories lost the record and his deeds do not appear.

units.zh: 梁開平三年，封朔方節度使韓遜為潁川王，始見於史。
units.en: In Liang Kaiping 3 Shuofang commissioner Han Xun was made Prince of Yingchuan—the first trace of him in the annals.
units.literal: In the third year of Kaiping of Liang, Shuofang military commissioner Han Xun was enfeoffed Prince of Yingchuan—this is his first appearance in the histories.

units.zh: 是時，邠寧楊崇本、鄜延李周彜、鳳翔李茂貞，皆與梁爭戰，獨遜與夏州李思諫臣屬於梁，未嘗以兵爭。
units.en: Yang Chongben of Bin, Li Zhouyi of Yan’an, and Li Maozhen of Fengxiang were all at war with Liang. Only Xun and Li Sijian of Xia bowed to Liang and kept the peace.
units.literal: At that time Binning’s Yang Chongben, Yan’an’s Li Zhouyi, and Fengxiang’s Li Maozhen all fought Liang; only Xun and Xia’s Li Sijian submitted to Liang and never contended with arms.

units.zh: 李茂貞嘗遣劉知俊攻遜，不能克，遜亦善撫其部，人皆愛之，為遜立生祠。
units.en: Maozhen sent Liu Zhijun against him and failed. Xun ruled his people gently; they loved him and raised living shrines in his name.
units.literal: Li Maozhen once sent Liu Zhijun to attack Xun and could not overcome him; Xun also knew how to soothe his tribes, and the people all loved him—they built him living shrines.

units.zh: 貞明中，遜卒，軍中立其子洙為留後，梁即以為節度使。
units.en: In the Zhenming era Xun died. The troops made his son Zhu acting commissioner, and Liang confirmed him.
units.literal: In the Zhenming era Xun died; the army set up his son Zhu as acting commissioner, and Liang at once made him military commissioner.

units.zh: 至莊宗時，又以洙兼河西節度。
units.en: Under Zhuangzong, Zhu also received the Hexi commission.
units.literal: By the time of Zhuangzong, Zhu was also given the Hexi commission.

units.zh: 天成四年，洙卒，即以洙子澄為朔方軍留後。
units.en: In Tiancheng 4 Zhu died; his son Cheng became acting commissioner of Shuofang.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancheng Zhu died, and Zhu’s son Cheng was made acting commissioner of the Shuofang army.

units.zh: 其將李賓作亂，澄乃上章請師於朝，明宗以康福為朔方河西節度使以代澄，由是命吏而相代矣。
units.en: General Li Bin mutinied. Cheng begged the court for help. Mingzong sent Kang Fu to replace him as commissioner of Shuofang and Hexi—the Han line ended and imperial appointees took over.
units.literal: His general Li Bin rebelled; Cheng then memorialized asking troops from court; Mingzong made Kang Fu Shuofang and Hexi military commissioner to replace Cheng—from this, appointed officials began to succeed one another.

units.zh: 韓氏自遜有靈武，傳世皆無所稱述，澄後不知其所終。
units.en: From Xun’s day at Lingwu the Hans left nothing worth a line in the histories. After Cheng, their fate is unknown.
units.literal: From Xun’s holding of Lingwu the Han house passed down the generations with nothing worth telling; after Cheng, how it ended is not known.

units.zh: 楊崇本
units.en: Yang Chongben
units.literal: Yang Chongben

units.zh: 楊崇本，幼事李茂貞，養以為子，冒姓李，名曰繼徽，茂貞表崇本靜難軍節度使。
units.en: Yang Chongben grew up in Li Maozhen's service, was adopted, took the Li surname and the name Jihui, and was made military commissioner of the Jingnan Army circuit.
units.literal: Yang Chongben in youth served Li Maozhen, was adopted as a son, took the surname Li, and was named Jihui; Maozhen memorialized Chongben as military commissioner of the Jingnan Army circuit.

units.zh: 梁太祖攻岐未下，乃移兵攻邠州，崇本迎降，太祖使復其姓，賜名崇本，遷其家於河中以為質。
units.en: Taizu could not crack Qi and turned on Bin. Chongben surrendered. Taizu restored his Yang surname, renamed him Chongben, and took his family to Hezhong as hostages.
units.literal: Liang Taizu attacked Qi and could not take it, then shifted troops to attack Bin; Chongben came out and surrendered; Taizu had him resume his original surname, bestowed the name Chongben, and moved his family to Hezhong as hostages.

units.zh: 崇本妻有美色，太祖用兵，往來河中，嘗幸之。
units.en: Chongben’s wife was famed for her beauty. Whenever Taizu marched through Hezhong he slept with her.
units.literal: Chongben’s wife was beautiful; when Taizu campaigned he often passed through Hezhong and took her to his bed.

units.zh: 崇本妻頗愧恥，間遣人誚崇本曰：「大丈夫不能庇其伉儷，我已為朱公婦矣，無面視君，有刀繩而已！」
units.en: Ashamed beyond bearing, she sent word: “What kind of man cannot protect his own wife? I am Zhu’s woman now. I cannot meet your eyes—only rope or steel remain!”
units.literal: Chongben’s wife was deeply ashamed; she sent someone to reproach Chongben: “A great man who cannot shield his wife—I am already Zhu Gong’s woman; I have no face to look on you; only blade and cord remain!”

units.zh: 崇本涕泣憤怒。
units.en: Chongben wept and raged.
units.literal: Chongben wept and burned with rage.

units.zh: 其後梁兵解岐圍，崇本妻得歸，崇本乃復背梁歸茂貞。
units.en: When Liang raised the siege of Qi his wife came home. Chongben broke with Liang and returned to Maozhen.
units.literal: Later Liang’s army lifted the siege of Qi; Chongben’s wife was able to return; Chongben then again turned against Liang and went back to Maozhen.

units.zh: 茂貞西連蜀兵會崇本攻雍、華，關西大震。
units.en: Maozhen allied with Shu in the west and, with Chongben, struck Yong and Hua. The land beyond the Pass trembled.
units.literal: Maozhen linked with Shu in the west; together with Chongben he attacked Yong and Hua, and the west of the Pass shook.

units.zh: 太祖以兵西至河中，遣郴王友裕擊之，友裕至永壽而卒，梁兵乃旋。
units.en: Taizu marched to Hezhong and sent Prince Youyu of Chen against them. Youyu died at Yongshou, and Liang turned back.
units.literal: Taizu marched west to Hezhong and sent the Prince of Chen, Youyu, to strike them; Youyu reached Yongshou and died; Liang’s army then withdrew.

units.zh: 崇本屯美原，太祖復遣劉知俊、康懷英等擊之，崇本大敗，自此不復東。
units.en: Chongben held Meiyuan. Taizu sent Liu Zhijun and Kang Huaiying against him and broke him so completely he never marched east again.
units.literal: Chongben camped at Meiyuan; Taizu again sent Liu Zhijun, Kang Huaiying, and others against him; Chongben was utterly defeated and from then on never marched east again.

units.zh: 乾化四年，為其子彥魯所殺。
units.en: In Qianhua 4 his son Yanlu murdered him.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Qianhua his son Yanlu killed him.

units.zh: 崇本養子李保衡，殺彥魯以降梁。
units.en: His adopted son Li Baoheng killed Yanlu and submitted to Liang.
units.literal: Chongben’s adopted son Li Baoheng killed Yanlu and surrendered to Liang.

units.zh: 高萬興
units.en: Gao Wanxing
units.literal: Gao Wanxing

units.zh: 高萬興，河西人也。
units.en: Gao Wanxing came from Hexi.
units.literal: Gao Wanxing was a man of Hexi.

units.zh: 唐末，河西屬李茂貞，茂貞將胡敬璋為延州刺史，萬興與其弟萬金俱事敬璋為騎將。
units.en: Late Tang Hexi lay under Li Maozhen. Maozhen’s Hu Jingzhang held Yan; Wanxing and his brother Wanjin served him as cavalry officers.
units.literal: At the end of Tang, Hexi belonged to Li Maozhen; Maozhen’s general Hu Jingzhang was military commissioner of Yan; Wanxing and his younger brother Wanjin both served Jingzhang as cavalry officers.

units.zh: 敬璋死，其將劉萬子代為刺史。
units.en: Jingzhang died. His officer Liu Wanzi became prefect.
units.literal: Jingzhang died; his general Liu Wanzi replaced him as prefect.

units.zh: 梁開平二年，葬於州南，萬子在會，其將許從實殺萬子，自為延州刺史。
units.en: In Liang Kaiping 2, as they buried Jingzhang south of the city, Wanzi was at the rites. Officer Xu Congshi killed him and seized Yan.
units.literal: In the second year of Kaiping of Liang, when they buried him south of the prefecture, Wanzi was at the funeral; his officer Xu Congshi killed Wanzi and made himself military commissioner of Yan.

units.zh: 是時，萬興兄弟皆將兵戍境上，聞萬子死，以其部下數千人，降梁。
units.en: The brothers were then on frontier duty. Hearing of Wanzi’s death, they led several thousand men to Liang.
units.literal: At that time the Wanxing brothers were both leading troops on the border; hearing Wanzi was dead, they brought several thousand men under them and surrendered to Liang.

units.zh: 梁太祖兵屯河中，遣同州劉知俊以兵應萬興，攻丹州，執其刺史崔公實。
units.en: Taizu was at Hezhong. He sent Liu Zhijun of Tong to join Wanxing, took Dan, and captured Prefect Cui Gongshi.
units.literal: Liang Taizu’s army was at Hezhong; he sent Liu Zhijun of Tong to support Wanxing, attacked Dan Prefecture, and seized its prefect Cui Gongshi.

units.zh: 進攻延州，執許從實。
units.en: They pressed on to Yan and took Xu Congshi.
units.literal: Advancing to attack Yan, they seized Xu Congshi.

units.zh: 鄜州李彥容、坊州李彥昱皆棄城走。
units.en: Li Yanrong of Fu Prefecture and Li Yanyu of Fang abandoned their posts and ran.
units.literal: Li Yanrong of Fu Prefecture and Li Yanyu of Fang both abandoned their cities and fled.

units.zh: 梁太祖乃以萬興為延州刺史、忠義軍節度使，以牛存節為保大軍節度使。
units.en: Taizu made Wanxing commissioner of Yan and the Zhongyi army, and Niu Cunjie commissioner of the Baoda army.
units.literal: Liang Taizu then made Wanxing military commissioner of Yan and the Zhongyi army, and Niu Cunjie military commissioner of the Baoda army.

units.zh: 已而劉知俊叛，乃徙存節守同州，以萬金為保大軍節度使。
units.en: Soon Liu Zhijun rebelled. Cunjie was shifted to Tong; Wanjin took Baoda.
units.literal: Before long Liu Zhijun rebelled; Cunjie was moved to guard Tong, and Wanjin was made military commissioner of the Baoda army.

units.zh: 萬興累遷檢校太師兼中書令，渤海郡王。
units.en: Wanxing rose to Acting Grand Preceptor, open-folder chancellor, and Prince of Bohai.
units.literal: Wanxing rose in office to Acting Grand Preceptor and co-equal with the Secretariat-Chancellery, Prince of Bohai commandery.

units.zh: 貞明四年，萬金卒，乃以萬興為鄜延節度使，進封延安郡王，徙封北平王。
units.en: In Zhenming 4 Wanjin died. Wanxing took Bianyan, was made Prince of Yan’an, then Prince of Beiping.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenming Wanjin died; Wanxing was then made military commissioner of Bianyan, advanced to Prince of Yan’an commandery, then transferred to Prince of Beiping.

units.zh: 梁亡，莊宗入洛，萬興嘗一來朝。
units.en: When Liang fell and Zhuangzong took Luoyang, Wanxing came to court once.
units.literal: When Liang fell and Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, Wanxing came once to court.

units.zh: 同光三年，卒於鎮。
units.en: He died in office in Tongguang 3.
units.literal: In the third year of Tongguang he died in his post.

units.zh: 萬興兄弟皆驍勇，而未嘗立戰功，然以戍兵降梁，梁取鄜、坊、丹、延自萬興始，故其兄弟世守其土。
units.en: The brothers were fierce riders who never won a famous battle—yet by leading frontier garrisons to Liang they handed Bin, Fang, Dan, and Yan to the dynasty, and their line held that country for generations.
units.literal: The Wanxing brothers were all fierce and brave, yet never won battle merit; but because they brought garrison troops to surrender to Liang, and Liang took Bin, Fang, Dan, and Yan beginning with Wanxing, therefore the brothers for generations held that soil.

units.zh: 萬興死，子允韜代立，長興元年徙鎮安國，又徙義成，清泰中卒。
units.en: Wanxing’s son Yuntao succeeded him, was shifted to Anguo in Changxing 1, then to Yicheng, and died in the Qingtai era.
units.literal: When Wanxing died his son Yuntao succeeded; in the first year of Changxing he was moved to govern Anguo, then Yicheng; he died in the Qingtai era.

units.zh: 萬金子允權，開運中為膚施令，罷居於家。
units.en: Wanjin’s son Yunquan was magistrate of Fushi under Later Jin’s Kaiyun era, then retired home.
units.literal: Wanjin’s son Yunquan, in the Kaiyun era, was magistrate of Fushi; removed, he lived at home.

units.zh: 是時，周密為彰信軍節度使，契丹滅晉，延州軍亂，逐密，密守東城，而西城之兵以允權為留後。
units.en: Zhou Mi held Zhangxin when the Khitan destroyed Jin. Yan’s garrison revolted, drove Mi into the eastern city, and made Yunquan acting commissioner in the west.
units.literal: At that time Zhou Mi was military commissioner of the Zhangxin army; the Khitan destroyed Jin; Yan’s army mutinied and drove Mi off; Mi held the eastern city while the western garrison made Yunquan acting commissioner.

units.zh: 聞漢高祖起太原，遂歸漢，即拜節度使，廣順三年卒。
units.en: When he heard Gaozu of Han was rising at Taiyuan he submitted and was confirmed commissioner; he died in Guangshun 3.
units.literal: Hearing that Gaozu of Han had risen at Taiyuan, he then submitted to Han and was at once appointed military commissioner; he died in the third year of Guangshun.

units.zh: 溫韜，京兆華原人也。
units.en: Wen Tao was from Huayuan in Jingzhao.
units.literal: Wen Tao, a native of Huayuan in Jingzhao.

units.zh: 少為盜，後事李茂貞，為華原鎮將，冒姓李，名彥韜。
units.en: As a youth he robbed on the roads. He entered Maozhen’s service, became garrison commander of Huayuan, took the Li surname, and was called Yanbiao.
units.literal: In youth he was a bandit; later he served Li Maozhen, became a garrison commander of Huayuan, took the surname Li, and was named Yanbiao.

units.zh: 茂貞以華原縣為耀州，以韜為刺史。
units.en: Maozhen raised Huayuan to Yao Prefecture and made Tao its prefect.
units.literal: Maozhen made Huayuan county into Yao Prefecture and appointed Tao prefect.

units.zh: 梁太祖圍茂貞於鳳翔，韜以耀州降梁，已而復叛歸茂貞。
units.en: Taizu besieged Maozhen at Fengxiang. Tao surrendered Yao, then rebelled back to Maozhen.
units.literal: Liang Taizu besieged Maozhen at Fengxiang; Tao surrendered Yao to Liang, then again rebelled and returned to Maozhen.

units.zh: 茂貞又以美原縣為鼎州，建義勝軍，以韜為節度使。
units.en: Maozhen then made Meiyuan into Ding Prefecture, created the Yisheng army, and made Tao its commissioner.
units.literal: Maozhen again made Meiyuan county into Ding Prefecture, established the Yisheng army, and made Tao its military commissioner.

units.zh: 末帝時，韜復叛茂貞降梁，梁改耀州為崇州，鼎州為裕州，義勝為靜勝軍，即以韜為節度使，復其姓溫，更其名曰昭圖。
units.en: Under the Last Emperor he broke with Maozhen again and joined Liang. Liang renamed Yao Chong, Ding Yu, and Yisheng Jingsheng; Tao kept the commission, took back the Wen surname, and was renamed Zhaotu.
units.literal: In the time of the Last Emperor, Tao again rebelled against Maozhen and surrendered to Liang; Liang changed Yao to Chong Prefecture, Ding to Yu Prefecture, Yisheng to the Jingsheng army, made Tao military commissioner, restored the surname Wen, and changed his name to Zhaotu.

units.zh: 韜在鎮七年，唐諸陵在其境內者，悉發掘之，取其所藏金寶，而昭陵最固，韜從埏道下，見宮室制度閎麗，不異人間，中為正寢，東西廂列石床，床上石函中為鐵匣，悉藏前世圖書，鐘、王筆跡，紙墨如新，韜悉取之，遂傳人間，惟乾陵風雨不可發。
units.en: Seven years he ruled that land. Every Tang imperial tomb in his circuit he plundered for its gold—but Zhaoling resisted him longest. He entered by the spirit tunnel and found halls as splendid as any palace: a central chamber, side rooms with stone couches, iron caskets within stone boxes holding ancient books and the calligraphy of Zhong Yao and Wang Xizhi, ink and paper fresh as the day they were laid in. He took everything. Only at Qianling did wind and rain turn his men back.
units.literal: Tao was in his post seven years; of the Tang imperial tombs within his territory he opened them all, took the gold and treasure stored there—and of them Zhaoling was the most secure; Tao went down the spirit passage, saw the palace halls grand and bright, no different from the human world; in the center was the main chamber, east and west wings lined with stone couches; on the couches stone caskets held iron cases, all storing books and maps of former ages, Zhong Yao’s and Wang Xizhi’s calligraphy traces; paper and ink were as new; Tao took them all, and they passed into the world—only Qianling, in wind and rain, could not be opened.

units.zh: 其後朱友謙叛梁，取同州，晉王以兵援友謙而趨華原，韜懼，求徙佗鎮，遂徙忠武。
units.en: When Zhu Youqian rebelled and took Tong, Jin marched to help him and threatened Huayuan. Tao begged a new post and was shifted to Zhongwu.
units.literal: Afterward Zhu Youqian rebelled against Liang and took Tong; the Jin Prince sent troops to aid Youqian and pressed toward Huayuan; Tao was afraid and asked transfer to another post, and was moved to Zhongwu.

units.zh: 莊宗滅梁，韜自許來朝，因伶人景進納賂劉皇后，皇后為言之，莊宗待韜甚厚，賜姓名曰李紹沖。
units.en: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Tao came from Xu to court, bribed Empress Liu through the actor Jing Jin, and won her word. Zhuangzong favored him lavishly and renamed him Li Shaochong.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Tao came from Xu to court; through the actor Jing Jin he bribed Empress Liu; the empress spoke for him; Zhuangzong treated Tao very generously and bestowed the surname and name Li Shaochong.

units.zh: 郭崇韜曰：「此劫陵賊爾，罪不可赦！」
units.en: Guo Chongtao said, “He is a tomb-robber. His crime admits no mercy!”
units.literal: Guo Chongtao said: “This is a tomb-robber; his crime cannot be pardoned!”

units.zh: 莊宗曰：「已宥之矣，不可失信。」
units.en: Zhuangzong said, “I have already spared him. A ruler cannot eat his word.”
units.literal: Zhuangzong said: “I have already forgiven him; faith cannot be broken.”

units.zh: 遽遣還鎮。
units.en: He sent him back to his command at once.
units.literal: He hurriedly sent him back to his post.

units.zh: 明宗入洛，與段凝俱收下獄，已而赦之，勒歸田里。
units.en: When Mingzong took Luoyang he and Duan Ning were thrown into prison, then pardoned and sent home.
units.literal: When Mingzong entered Luoyang, he and Duan Ning were both seized and put in prison; before long they were pardoned and ordered to return to their villages.

units.zh: 明年，流於德州，賜死。
units.en: The next year he was exiled to Dezhou and granted death.
units.literal: The next year he was exiled to Dezhou and ordered to die.

units.zh: 嗚呼，厚葬之弊，自秦漢已來，率多聰明英偉之主，雖有高談善說之士，極陳其禍福，有不能開其惑者矣！
units.en: Alas—the curse of rich tombs! Since Qin and Han it has chiefly seduced the clever and the bold. Eloquent men preached disaster in vain; they could not pierce the delusion.
units.literal: Alas! The harm of lavish burial—from Qin and Han down, it has mostly been intelligent and heroic rulers; though eloquent men urgently set forth its fortune and calamity, they could not open such rulers’ delusion!

units.zh: 豈非富貴之欲，溺其所自私者篤，而未然之禍，難述於無形，不足以動其心歟？
units.en: Men drown in the wish for glory while the unseen ruin ahead has no shape to frighten them—how should it stir the heart?
units.literal: Is it not that the desire for wealth and rank drowns what one cherishes for oneself, and calamity not yet come, hard to describe in what has no form, is not enough to move the heart?

units.zh: 然而聞溫韜之事者，可以少戒也！
units.en: Yet Wen Tao’s story might warn even the stubborn a little.
units.literal: Yet those who hear of Wen Tao’s affair may take a little warning!

units.zh: 五代之君，往往不得其死，何暇顧其後哉！
units.en: Five Dynasties emperors rarely died in bed. Who had leisure to plan for the dead?
units.literal: The rulers of the Five Dynasties often did not die in their beds—how could they spare thought for what came after?

units.zh: 獨周太祖能鑒韜之禍，其將終也，為書以遺世宗，使以瓦棺、紙衣而斂。
units.en: Only Zhou Taizu took Tao’s lesson to heart. On his deathbed he wrote Shizong: bury me in a tile coffin clad in paper.
units.literal: Only Zhou Taizu could take warning from Tao’s calamity; as he was about to die he wrote a letter to Shizong, telling him to bury the body in a tile coffin with paper garments.

units.zh: 將葬，開棺示人，既葬，刻石以告後世，毋作下宮，毋置守陵妾。
units.en: Before burial he opened the coffin for all to see, then carved stone for posterity: no underground palace, no concubines to guard the mound.
units.literal: When he was about to be buried he opened the coffin to show the people; after burial he carved stone to tell posterity: make no lower palace, set no tomb-guarding concubines.

units.zh: 其意丁寧切至，然實錄不書其葬之薄厚也。
units.en: He meant every word—and still the veritable record does not say whether the grave was humble or grand.
units.literal: His intent was earnest and urgent to the utmost, yet the veritable record does not state whether the burial was spare or lavish.

units.zh: 又使葬其平生所服袞冕、通天冠、絳紗袍各二，其一於京師，其一於澶州；
units.en: He also had duplicate sets of the regalia he had worn in life—the full court dress, the Tongtian crown, the crimson gauze gown—buried two of each, one at the capital and one at Chunzhou;
units.literal: Again he also had buried the court robes of state, the Tongtian crown, and the crimson gauze robes he had worn through his life, two of each—one set at the capital, one at Chunzhou;

units.zh: 又葬其劍、甲各二，其一於河中，其一於大名者，莫能原其旨也。
units.en: The same for his sword and armor: two of each, one laid in the earth at Hezhong, one at Daming. None could read what he meant.
units.literal: Again he buried his sword and armor, two of each, one at Hezhong and one at Daming—and no one could fathom his purpose.
